subject: Mutual acceptance handshake: success signals, exit gates & test harness
messages:
From: Alex Green <alex.green@nexerahealth.com>

Subject: Initial ask: acceptance criteria for eval + timeline

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and cost numbers look promising. We need to lock down a short, operational MAP so we can run an internal evaluation with engineering and procurement. Specifically:

- A concise list of what success looks like (quant & qual).
- Clear exit gates / rollback triggers.
- An acceptance-test harness we can run from our side (smoke tests + sample prompt set).
- A proposed two-week timeline for the evaluation and an estimate for guardrail support from your side (who will run what).

We’re trying to get procurement comfortable before EOW and want to avoid back-and-forth. Can you send a single doc that lays this out? If possible include a simple scoring rubric we can use to greenlight a pilot.

cc: procurement@nexerahealth.com, dana.li@nexerahealth.com

Alex
Principal Product Manager
Nexera Health
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@nexerahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-21T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: acceptance criteria for eval + timeline

Alex — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a concise MAP (MAP_Nexera_v1.xlsx) and a short eval-smoke-harness doc that outlines test cases and ownership. High-level summary below so procurement has something short to read.

Quick summary (proposed):
- Success signals (must-haves):
  • Latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 450ms for 256 token prompts (test harness measured).
  • Conformance: intent classification F1 >= 0.92 on provided label set (50 sample cases).
  • Safety/stability: hallucination rate (as defined in doc) < 2% on 200 random prompts.
  • Cost guardrail: per-transaction cost within 20% of the POC estimate in the attached MAP.
- Exit gates (fail-fast):
  • If latency 95p > 700ms on production-like traffic pattern after two tuning cycles.
  • If hallucination rate > 5% on continuous test after mitigations.
  • If critical data-residency/logging requirements cannot be met (see procurement asks).
- Acceptance tests:
  • Smoke harness (attached): integration basic flow, concurrency ramp to 200 rps, sample prompt QA, embedding similarity checks.
  • Ownership: Redwood runs the first full smoke run with Nexera engineers on call; Nexera runs subsequent runs independently.
- Timeline (recommended):
  • Day 0: MAP sign-off and kickoff.
  • Day 1–3: infra & sample data ingest + baseline smoke run.
  • Day 4–10: targeted improvements (batching/quantization, cache rules), two measurement runs.
  • Day 11–14: final verification & sign-off or rollback decision.

I’ve called out specific artifacts and who is responsible in the MAP. Can we do a quick 30-min sync tomorrow to walk procurement through the acceptance gates? If procurement needs a separate appendix on audit/logging we can add it.

—Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_Nexera_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), eval-smoke-harness.md (text)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22T08:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: acceptance criteria for eval + timeline — acceptance tests (detailed)

Looping in detailed acceptance tests for the MAP — put this in the "eval-smoke-harness.md" (excerpt below). We should be explicit about measurement methods so there are no surprises.

Acceptance-test excerpts (operationalized):

1) Latency suite
- Tool: k6 load profile (script in repo).
- Metric: 95th percentile for total token generation (end-to-end) measured across 3 runs with 15-min steady-state windows.
- Pass: 95p < 450ms in at least 2/3 runs; Warning if 450–700ms; Fail if > 700ms after two tuning cycles.

2) Accuracy & concordance
- Tool: Redwood eval harness + Nexera golden set (n=50).
- Metric: Intent classification F1 and free-text BLEU-ish concordance (we use a thresholded fuzzy-match).
- Pass: F1 >= 0.92 AND concordance score >= 0.84.

3) Hallucination / safety checks
- Method: Mix of automated classifiers + 200 human spot checks.
- Pass: Automated flagging < 3% and human-confirmed hallucination rate < 2%.

4) Embeddings stability (if used for search/rerank)
- Check: cosine similarity over canonical pairs; pass threshold >= 0.82 median.

5) Reliability / resilience
- Scenario tests: instance preemption, traffic spikes (x5 baseline), partial model fallback.
- Rollback triggers: repeated repeated failures or SLO violations after two mitigation efforts.

Rollback playbook (short):
- If a fail gate trips, we pause rollout, revert to the prior model variant, and run a 24-hour verification window.
- If issue persists, schedule an executive review (Rishi + Nexera engineering lead + CSM).

Operational notes for procurement appendix: data residency controls, retention windows (30/90/365 day options), and audit log export cadence. I added these to the MAP spreadsheet. Recommend we assign Dana from Nexera as the procurement reviewer.

—Marissa
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs referenced: eval-smoke-harness.md (contains k6 scripts, sample prompts, and scoring script).
